Tráfico en CDMX dispara el estrés y la ira al volante: así afecta a los conductores

2026-07-31 Samantha Godínez (Infobae) TomTom Traffic, CDMX, congestion, road rage, urban mobility, traffic stress
Read the source article

Quick summary

Mexico City reached 75.9% congestion in 2025 per TomTom Traffic data, making it one of the world's most congested cities and triggering severe psychological impacts on drivers including road rage.

Key takeaways

  • CDMX achieved 75.9% congestion level in 2025 according to TomTom Traffic data, surpassing Bangalore, Dublin, and Bogotá.
  • Average driving speed is 17.4 km/h, meaning drivers cover only 4.3 km in 15 minutes.
  • Psychologists from UNAM link traffic-induced stress to clinical road rage, with impulsivity and low emotional control as key risk factors.
  • Environmental factors—heat, noise, fatigue, and work stress—compound the psychological toll of prolonged commutes.
  • The phenomenon extends beyond inconvenience to become a public safety issue, with aggressive driving threatening all road users.
